title: Injuries in runners; a systematic review on risk factors and sex differences
authors: van der Worp MP, ten Haaf DS, van Cingel R, de Wijer A, Nijhuis-van der Sanden MW, Staal JB
population: 15 longitudinal cohort studies of runners with at least 1 month follow-up (11 high quality, 4 moderate quality)
findings: 15 longitudinal studies were included out of 400 retrieved; 11 were rated high quality and 4 moderate quality.
Strong and moderate evidence was found that a history of previous injury and having used orthotics/inserts were associated with increased injury risk.
Overall, women were at lower risk than men for sustaining running-related injuries; the review notes the risk profile appeared to differ by sex but few studies reported sexes separately.
Authors caution that results should be interpreted carefully because of recall bias, follow-up time and participation rates.
limitations: Best-evidence synthesis without pooling; few studies reported results by sex; its 'women at lower risk' conclusion differs from the later Hollander 2021 meta-analysis (no overall sex difference).
implications: Supports a previous-injury flag as the best-supported general (non-training) risk factor for running injury.
Do not use sex to change overall volume limits (conflicting evidence, see Hollander 2021).
